intent.raw_query: Costa Rica eco-adventure, $2500, zip-lining and wildlife, February 2026 from Miami

experiences.name: Monteverde Cloud Forest Zip-Line Canopy Tour
experiences.description: Soar through the misty cloud forest canopy on one of Costa Rica's most thrilling zip-line circuits, featuring 15 cables, Tarzan swings, and breathtaking views of the Monteverde reserve. Spot toucans, howler monkeys, and exotic orchids along the way.

experiences.name: Tortuguero National Park Wildlife Boat Safari
experiences.description: Glide through the jungle canals of Tortuguero on a guided boat safari teeming with caimans, river turtles, three-toed sloths, poison dart frogs, and over 300 bird species. Depending on the season, witness the awe-inspiring nesting of green sea turtles on the beach.

experiences.name: Arenal Volcano Hanging Bridges Hike
experiences.description: Trek through primary rainforest on a network of 16 hanging bridges suspended high above the forest floor, offering panoramic views of Arenal Volcano and incredible wildlife encounters including poison dart frogs, coatis, and resplendent quetzals.

experiences.name: Manuel Antonio Beach and Wildlife Snorkel Experience
experiences.description: Combine a relaxing afternoon on the pristine white-sand beaches of Manuel Antonio National Park with a guided snorkeling session in the warm Pacific waters. Encounter white-faced capuchin monkeys, sloths, and colorful reef fish just steps from the shoreline.

experiences.name: Corcovado National Park Guided Jungle Trek
experiences.description: Explore one of the most biodiverse places on Earth with a certified naturalist guide deep into Corcovado's old-growth rainforest. Encounter tapirs, scarlet macaws, white-lipped peccaries, and jaguar tracks on this immersive full-day eco-adventure in the Osa Peninsula.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Costa Rica
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled - flight arrives at 13:00
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Juan Santamaría International Airport at 13:00. Clear customs, exchange currency or withdraw colones from airport ATM for better rates. Take the affordable public bus or shared shuttle to Aegean Bliss Resort (budget tip: avoid airport taxis which charge premium rates). Check in, freshen up, and explore the beachfront property and surrounding area on foot.
day_by_day.evening: Take a leisurely sunset walk along the beach near the resort. Get oriented with the local neighborhood, locate nearby sodas (local budget eateries) and mini-supermarkets for snacks and water.

meals.breakfast: Eat before or during the flight
meals.lunch: Grab a casado (rice, beans, meat, salad) at a local soda near the airport or bus terminal for around $5-7 USD
meals.dinner: Find a nearby local soda or beachside casual restaurant for a traditional gallo pinto with chicken or fish for $6-10 USD

day_by_day.notes: Day 1 is purely arrival and orientation. Prioritize rest and hydration. Pick up a SIM card at the airport (Kolbi or Claro) for affordable data. Budget tip: a public bus from San José to the coast costs under $5 USD versus $80+ for private transfers.

day_by_day.morning: Wake up early for a sunrise beach walk to spot shorebirds, pelicans, and possibly sea turtles near the waterline. Visit the local fish market if available near the resort area. Enjoy a budget breakfast at the resort or a nearby soda.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the local town on foot or by bicycle rental ($5-10/day). Visit any nearby national park visitor center or ranger station to get free maps and wildlife information. Look for free or low-cost wildlife viewing spots such as mangrove edges or riverbanks where you might spot crocodiles, iguanas, and tropical birds.
day_by_day.evening: Head back to the beachfront for a relaxed evening. Chat with other budget travelers at the resort to exchange tips. Watch for bioluminescence in the water if conditions are right.

meals.breakfast: Gallo pinto with eggs and fresh fruit juice at a local soda — $3-5 USD
meals.lunch: Casado del día (plate of the day) at a local soda — $5-7 USD
meals.dinner: Self-catered meal from local supermarket: fresh bread, local cheese, fruits, and snacks — $4-6 USD

day_by_day.notes: February is dry season on the Pacific coast — expect sunny skies and warm temperatures around 28-32°C (82-90°F). Apply sunscreen generously. Stay hydrated with bottled or filtered water.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning wildlife walk in a nearby forest trail or biological reserve. Look for howler monkeys, sloths, toucans, and scarlet macaws which are commonly spotted in coastal forest areas. Bring binoculars if available (some hostels lend them free).
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a local waterfall or swimming hole accessible by public bus or on foot. Many coastal areas of Costa Rica have free-access natural swimming spots. Alternatively, explore tide pools at low tide for marine wildlife observation.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a free or low-cost cultural event in the local town square if available. Otherwise, enjoy the beachfront at the resort and stargaze — Costa Rica's dry season skies are spectacular.

meals.breakfast: Fruit bowl with granola and local coffee at a soda — $3-4 USD
meals.lunch: Arroz con pollo or fresh fish tacos from a beachside stand — $4-6 USD
meals.dinner: Local soda dinner: whole fried fish with rice, beans, and salad — $8-10 USD

day_by_day.notes: Wildlife tip: early mornings (6:00-8:00 AM) are the best time to spot animals as they are most active. Move quietly and slowly on trails. Wear neutral-colored clothing to avoid startling wildlife.

day_by_day.morning: Take a half-day guided or self-guided mangrove kayak tour. Many areas offer affordable kayak rentals ($15-25 for a half day) where you can paddle through mangroves and spot crocodiles, herons, kingfishers, and monkeys from the water.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return from kayaking and rest during the hottest part of the day (12:00-2:00 PM). Visit a local artisan market or souvenir stalls to browse handmade crafts. Budget tip: prices are negotiable and locally made goods support the community.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a beach bonfire if permitted, or join other travelers for a casual evening on the sand. Look for free live music at local bars near the beach.

meals.breakfast: Pinto with natilla (sour cream) and fresh tropical juice — $3-5 USD at a local soda
meals.lunch: Pack a picnic lunch from the supermarket: fruits, crackers, cheese, and local snacks — $3-5 USD
meals.dinner: Ceviche and patacones (fried plantains) at a casual beachside restaurant — $7-9 USD

day_by_day.notes: Mangrove kayaking is one of Costa Rica's best budget eco-adventures. Always wear a life jacket and bring waterproof sunscreen. Protect your phone in a waterproof bag.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to a nearby national park or wildlife refuge. Many of Costa Rica's parks charge $10-18 USD entrance fees for foreigners — well worth it for incredible biodiversity. Explore trails on your own to save on guide fees. Look for sloths, monkeys, coatis, and hundreds of bird species.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring the national park. If near the coast, visit the park's beach sections which are often pristine and less crowded than public beaches. Swim, snorkel (bring or rent cheap snorkel gear), and look for sea turtles.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort by public bus or shared shuttle. Relax and recap the day's wildlife sightings. Write or photograph your nature journal entries.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the resort or a soda before departure — $3-5 USD
meals.lunch: Bring packed lunch into the park to avoid expensive park concession prices: sandwiches, fruit, nuts — $4-5 USD
meals.dinner: Treat yourself to a slightly nicer local restaurant after the full day out — grilled sea bass with coconut rice — $10-13 USD

day_by_day.notes: Bring at least 2 liters of water per person into the park. Trails can be muddy even in dry season near rivers. Wear closed-toe shoes or waterproof sandals. Entrance fees are often cash only.

day_by_day.morning: ZIP-LINING DAY! Book an affordable zip-line tour in advance — Costa Rica has dozens of operators ranging from $30-80 USD. Look for smaller local operators rather than large commercial ones for better prices and more personal experiences. Briefing and safety equipment fitting in the morning.
day_by_day.afternoon: Complete the zip-line circuit — most tours include 8-15 platforms through the forest canopy, offering incredible views and wildlife sightings from above. Some tours include a hanging bridges walk or rappelling as add-ons.
day_by_day.evening: Celebrate your zip-lining adventure! Enjoy a cold Imperial beer (Costa Rica's local brew) or fresh coconut water at a beachside bar. Share photos and stories with fellow travelers.

meals.breakfast: Light breakfast before the tour — banana, granola bar, and coffee — $2-3 USD
meals.lunch: Many zip-line tours include a basic lunch; if not, eat at the tour operator's nearby soda — $5-7 USD
meals.dinner: Celebrate with a communal dinner at a local restaurant: BBQ chicken, rice and beans, and fresh salad — $8-10 USD

day_by_day.notes: Book zip-lining at least 2-3 days in advance especially in February (high season). Weight limits typically apply (usually 100-120kg max). Wear closed-toe shoes, no loose jewelry. GoPro or action camera rentals are often available at the tour desk for $10-15 extra.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and recovery morning after the active zip-lining day. Sleep in, enjoy a slow breakfast, and do gentle stretching on the beach. Read, journal, or simply enjoy the sound of the ocean.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore a local wildlife rescue center or sanctuary — many charge $10-20 USD admission and allow close-up encounters with rescued sloths, monkeys, birds, and reptiles. These centers also do important conservation work your fee supports.
day_by_day.evening: Night wildlife walk along the beach or forest edge. February evenings may offer sea turtle nesting activity depending on the specific coastal location. Look for ghost crabs, nocturnal insects, and listen for owl and frog calls.

meals.breakfast: Leisurely breakfast at a café: pancakes with local honey and fresh fruit — $4-6 USD
meals.lunch: Smoothie bowl or fresh fruit plate from a health-food stand — $4-6 USD
meals.dinner: Local soda comfort food: sopa negra (black bean soup) with egg and rice — $5-7 USD

day_by_day.notes: Day 7 is intentionally lighter to prevent burnout on a 13-day trip. Budget travelers often forget to build in rest days which leads to exhaustion. Stay hydrated and use reef-safe sunscreen to protect Costa Rica's marine ecosystems.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning bird watching walk — Costa Rica is one of the world's top birding destinations with over 900 species. Download the free Merlin Bird ID app before the trip. Target species include toucans, motmots, trogons, and the iconic Scarlet Macaw.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a local organic farm or permaculture project — many offer free or low-cost tours showing sustainable agriculture, tropical fruit trees, and medicinal plants. Great insight into Costa Rican rural life and eco-practices.
day_by_day.evening: Cook a communal meal at the resort if kitchen facilities are available, using fresh local ingredients from a nearby market. A great way to save money and socialize with other travelers.

meals.breakfast: Grab-and-go from a bakery: fresh pan de yuca (cassava bread) and local coffee — $2-3 USD
meals.lunch: Farm tour may include a traditional meal or snacks; otherwise eat at a nearby soda — $5-7 USD
meals.dinner: Self-cooked meal with fresh local vegetables, rice, beans, and plantains from the market — $3-5 USD per person

day_by_day.notes: The Merlin Bird ID app by Cornell Lab is completely free and works offline — essential for budget birders. Many serious birders hire guides but self-guided birding with the app is highly effective and free.

day_by_day.morning: Take a public bus or shared shuttle to a different beach or coastal area within reach of the resort for a change of scenery. Costa Rica's Pacific coast has diverse beach environments from surf beaches to calm coves.
day_by_day.afternoon: Snorkeling or boogie boarding at the new beach location. Cheap boogie boards can be rented for $5-10/hour at most beach towns. Look for colorful reef fish, sea urchins, and starfish in rocky tide pools.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort by public bus. Enjoy a sunset happy hour at a local beach bar — many offer 2-for-1 drinks during happy hour (typically 4:00-6:00 PM).

meals.breakfast: Eat before departure: gallo pinto and eggs at the resort area soda — $3-5 USD
meals.lunch: Fresh ceviche or fish tacos from a beachside vendor at the new location — $5-8 USD
meals.dinner: Happy hour snacks (nachos, empanadas) paired with a cold beer or fresh agua de pipa (coconut water) — $5-8 USD

day_by_day.notes: Public buses in Costa Rica are extremely affordable ($1-4 USD for most regional routes) and a great way to meet locals. Google Maps works well for bus route planning in Costa Rica. Always have small colones bills for the bus fare.

day_by_day.morning: White-water rafting or river tubing excursion — one of Costa Rica's top eco-adventures. Budget operators offer half-day river tubing for $20-35 USD, much cheaper than full rafting. Rivers in February have good flow levels.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the river activity, visit a nearby waterfall accessible by a short hike. Many of Costa Rica's most beautiful waterfalls are free or charge minimal fees ($2-5 USD). Cool off with a swim in the natural pool.
day_by_day.evening: Relaxed evening at the resort. Share your day's adventure photos, plan remaining days, and do any laundry (many budget accommodations have self-service laundry for $2-4 USD).

meals.breakfast: Light pre-activity breakfast: banana, granola bar, and coffee — $2-3 USD
meals.lunch: Post-river lunch at a riverside soda: casado with fresh juice — $5-7 USD
meals.dinner: Beachfront dinner: grilled chicken with chimichurri, rice, and plantains — $8-10 USD

day_by_day.notes: River activities require closed-toe shoes (water shoes or old sneakers work well). Do not bring valuables — most operators provide waterproof bags for phones. Check operator safety ratings and ensure they provide helmets and life jackets.

day_by_day.morning: Morning yoga or meditation on the beach — many resorts and local instructors offer free or donation-based morning sessions. A wonderful way to connect with nature and recharge. Alternatively, take a solo sunrise meditation walk.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a local fishing village or marina to watch fishermen bring in their catch. Many will sell fresh fish directly at very low prices. Learn about traditional fishing methods and Costa Rican coastal culture.
day_by_day.evening: Cook fresh fish purchased from the fishermen (if kitchen available) or ask a local soda to prepare it for you for a small fee — a uniquely authentic experience.

meals.breakfast: Tropical fruit platter with local coffee at a beachside café — $3-5 USD
meals.lunch: Ceviche made with fresh catch from the fishing village — $4-6 USD at a local vendor
meals.dinner: Fresh locally purchased fish prepared simply: grilled with garlic, lemon, rice, and salad — $4-7 USD total if self-cooked

day_by_day.notes: Day 11 focuses on cultural immersion and slow travel. Budget travel is enriched by genuine local interactions. Learning a few Spanish phrases (¿Cuánto cuesta? — How much does it cost? / Muchas gracias — Thank you very much) goes a long way with locals.

day_by_day.morning: Final major eco-adventure: horseback riding through coastal forest or to a waterfall. Local ranches offer 2-3 hour rides for $25-45 USD — a memorable way to experience the landscape and spot wildlife from a different vantage point.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return from horseback riding and spend the afternoon at the beach. Collect memories, take final photos, and enjoy the ocean. Consider renting a stand-up paddleboard (SUP) for $10-15/hour for a final water adventure.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner with other travelers you've met during the trip. Choose a slightly nicer local restaurant to celebrate the journey — still budget-friendly but a small splurge for the final full evening.

meals.breakfast: Hearty breakfast before the ride: eggs, gallo pinto, toast, and fresh juice — $4-6 USD
meals.lunch: Picnic on the beach or at the ranch: local fruits, sandwiches, and agua fresca — $3-5 USD
meals.dinner: Celebratory dinner: whole lobster or jumbo shrimp with coconut rice and plantains — $12-18 USD (splurge night!)

day_by_day.notes: Horseback riding operators should be vetted for animal welfare standards — choose operators where horses appear well-fed and cared for. The Association of Responsible Tourism in Costa Rica (ACTUARIA) can help identify ethical operators.

day_by_day.morning: Final sunrise walk on the beach — take it all in one last time. Spot any remaining wildlife: frigate birds soaring overhead, hermit crabs on the sand, and the ever-present howler monkeys in the trees. Pack your bags and check out of the resort.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on departure flight time, either take a final dip in the ocean or head toward the airport. Allow extra travel time — Costa Rica's roads can be slow. Take the public bus or pre-booked shared shuttle to San José airport. Do final souvenir shopping at the airport duty-free or local shops en route.
day_by_day.evening: Depart Costa Rica with incredible memories of zip-lining through the canopy, wildlife encounters, river adventures, and the pura vida lifestyle. ¡Pura Vida!

meals.breakfast: Final gallo pinto breakfast at a local soda — $3-5 USD (a fitting farewell to Costa Rica's national dish)
meals.lunch: Light meal at the airport or en route: empanadas and fresh juice — $5-8 USD
meals.dinner: Airport meal or on the flight

day_by_day.notes: BUDGET SUMMARY TIPS: Total estimated daily budget $40-65 USD/person (excluding accommodation) is achievable. Key savings: public buses over private transfers, sodas over tourist restaurants, self-guided over guided tours where possible, and supermarket snacks for lunches. Costa Rica's 'pura vida' philosophy is about enjoying life simply — the best experiences here are often free: wildlife, sunsets, and genuine local connections.

trip_options.title: Classic Costa Rica Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

experiences.name: Monteverde Cloud Forest Zip-Line Canopy Tour
experiences.description: Soar through the misty cloud forest canopy on one of Costa Rica's most thrilling zip-line circuits, featuring 15 cables, Tarzan swings, and breathtaking views of the Monteverde reserve. Spot toucans, howler monkeys, and exotic orchids along the way.

experiences.name: Tortuguero National Park Wildlife Boat Safari
experiences.description: Glide through the jungle canals of Tortuguero on a guided boat safari teeming with caimans, river turtles, three-toed sloths, poison dart frogs, and over 300 bird species. Depending on the season, witness the awe-inspiring nesting of green sea turtles on the beach.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — flight arrives at 13:00
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Juan Santamaría International Airport at 13:00. Clear customs, collect luggage, and arrange private shuttle or shared transfer to Aegean Bliss Resort on the beachfront (approximately 2–3 hours depending on location). Check in, freshen up, and take a leisurely stroll along the beach to get oriented.
day_by_day.evening: Relax at the resort, enjoy the sunset from the beachfront. Light exploration of the resort amenities and surrounding area.

meals.breakfast: On the plane or at the airport
meals.lunch: Grab a quick bite at the airport — Soda Tapia near SJO offers affordable traditional Costa Rican casados (rice, beans, protein) for around $8–12
meals.dinner: Dinner at the resort restaurant — try the fresh catch of the day with patacones (fried plantains) and a local Imperial beer. Budget ~$20–30 per person

day_by_day.notes: Exchange some currency to Costa Rican Colones at the airport (Banco Nacional kiosk inside arrivals). Keep arrival day light — jet lag and travel fatigue are real. Confirm next-day activities with the resort concierge.

day_by_day.morning: Wake up early and join a guided sunrise beach walk with a local naturalist guide (~2 hours). Look for shorebirds, hermit crabs, and possibly nesting sea turtles depending on the season. This is a perfect gentle introduction to Costa Rica's coastal wildlife.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to a nearby estuary or mangrove reserve for a 2-hour kayaking tour through mangrove channels. Spot herons, kingfishers, crocodiles, and howler monkeys from the water. Most beachfront areas in Costa Rica have operators offering this for $40–60 per person.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort, shower, and head into the nearest beach town for dinner. Explore the local sodas (small family restaurants) along the main strip.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast buffet or a nearby soda — gallo pinto (rice and beans with egg), fresh tropical fruit, and coffee. ~$8–12
meals.lunch: Pack a light snack for the kayaking tour or stop at a beachside rancho for ceviche and coconut water. ~$10–15
meals.dinner: Dinner at a local soda in town — order a traditional casado with chicken or fish, fresh juice, and dessert. ~$12–18 per person

day_by_day.notes: Apply sunscreen and insect repellent before all outdoor activities. Bring a dry bag for the kayaking tour to protect your phone and camera. Book the mangrove kayak tour the evening before through the resort concierge.

day_by_day.morning: Full-day excursion begins: depart early (6:00–7:00 AM) by private shuttle toward Tortuguero National Park. The journey involves road travel to the embarkation point (Cariari or La Pavona) followed by a scenic 1.5-hour boat ride through jungle waterways to reach Tortuguero village.
day_by_day.afternoon: Tortuguero National Park Wildlife Boat Safari — glide through the jungle canals on a guided boat safari teeming with caimans, river turtles, river otters, three species of monkeys, sloths, toucans, and over 400 bird species. This is one of Costa Rica's premier wildlife experiences. Tour lasts approximately 2–3 hours.
day_by_day.evening: Check into a mid-range lodge in Tortuguero village (pre-booked — options include Manatus Hotel or Tortuga Lodge at $80–150/night). Enjoy a guided night walk along the jungle trails to spot nocturnal wildlife including frogs, insects, and sleeping birds.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the resort before departure — grab fruit and coffee to go if needed
meals.lunch: Lunch at a local restaurant in Tortuguero village — fresh fish soup or rice and beans Caribbean style. ~$10–15
meals.dinner: Dinner at the lodge restaurant or a village eatery — try Caribbean-style rice and beans cooked in coconut milk with jerk chicken. ~$15–22 per person

day_by_day.notes: Tortuguero is only accessible by boat or small plane — there are no roads into the park. Pack light for this overnight excursion. Bring rain gear as Tortuguero is one of the rainiest places in Costa Rica. Book boat safari and lodge well in advance. Overnight stay in Tortuguero.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning second wildlife canal boat tour (6:00–8:00 AM) — mornings offer the best wildlife activity. Look for Jesus Christ lizards running across the water, fresh-water turtles basking, and spectacular birdlife including kingfishers, anhingas, and roseate spoonbills.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Sea Turtle Conservancy Visitor Center in Tortuguero village to learn about the park's legendary sea turtle nesting programs (green turtles nest July–October, leatherbacks March–April). Walk the village, browse local artisan crafts, and relax before the return journey. Depart Tortuguero by boat back to the mainland and transfer by shuttle back toward the resort.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive back at Aegean Bliss Resort by early evening. Rest, swim in the ocean or pool, and enjoy a quiet dinner at the resort.

meals.breakfast: Lodge breakfast — eggs, gallo pinto, fresh fruit, and coffee before the morning tour
meals.lunch: Pack snacks for the return journey or stop at a roadside soda en route — rice dishes, empanadas, and fresh juice. ~$8–12
meals.dinner: Resort restaurant dinner — try the grilled mahi-mahi with chimichurri and yuca fries. ~$20–28 per person

day_by_day.notes: The return journey from Tortuguero can take 3–4 hours total including boat and shuttle. Depart Tortuguero no later than 1:00–2:00 PM to arrive at the resort before dark. Confirm return shuttle timing with your Tortuguero lodge the night before.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and recovery day after the Tortuguero excursion. Enjoy a slow breakfast and a morning swim in the ocean. Alternatively, take a yoga or meditation class if offered at the resort (many Costa Rican beach resorts offer complimentary or low-cost morning yoga sessions).
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a nearby wildlife rescue center or animal sanctuary (common near most Costa Rican beach towns). These centers rehabilitate sloths, monkeys, toucans, and other injured wildlife. Entry is typically $15–25 and directly supports conservation efforts. Spend 2–3 hours exploring.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset horseback ride along the beach — a quintessential Costa Rica experience. Many local operators offer 1.5 to 2-hour rides along the shoreline for $40–60 per person. Return for a beachfront dinner.

meals.breakfast: Leisurely resort breakfast — fresh smoothie bowls, tropical fruit platter, and local coffee. ~$10–15
meals.lunch: Beachside lunch at a casual rancho or food truck — fresh ceviche, tostones, and a cold drink. ~$12–16
meals.dinner: Dinner at a mid-range beachfront restaurant — try the whole fried snapper with rice, beans, and a salad. ~$18–25 per person

day_by_day.notes: Book the horseback ride in advance through the resort or a local tour operator. Wear closed-toe shoes for horseback riding. The wildlife rescue center visit is a great opportunity for photography — bring your camera with a zoom lens.

day_by_day.morning: Depart early for Monteverde Cloud Forest — one of Costa Rica's most iconic destinations. The drive takes approximately 3–4 hours from most beach areas (including a scenic ferry crossing over Lake Arenal if coming from the Pacific coast). Arrive and check into a mid-range Monteverde lodge (options include Monteverde Inn or Arco Iris Lodge at $60–100/night).
day_by_day.afternoon: After checking in and having lunch, visit the Monteverde Cloud Forest Biological Reserve for a self-guided or guided afternoon hike (2–3 hours). Walk through mystical cloud forest draped in moss and orchids. Spot resplendent quetzals (peak season February–April), three-wattled bellbirds, and glass frogs. Entry fee ~$25.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a guided night tour of the cloud forest or a frog pond tour to spot nocturnal species including red-eyed tree frogs, tarantulas, and stick insects. These tours run approximately 2 hours and cost $25–35 per person.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the resort before departure — pack snacks for the road
meals.lunch: Lunch in Santa Elena town (the gateway to Monteverde) — try Morpho's Restaurant for traditional Costa Rican food with vegetarian options. ~$12–18
meals.dinner: Dinner at Restaurante Sabor Tico in Santa Elena — hearty casados, fresh salads, and homemade desserts. ~$14–20 per person

day_by_day.notes: Overnight stay in Monteverde. The roads to Monteverde are famously rough and unpaved in sections — a 4WD vehicle is recommended. Bring a light fleece or jacket as Monteverde averages 65–72°F (18–22°C) and can be misty and cool. Book the night tour in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Monteverde Cloud Forest Zip-Line Canopy Tour — the highlight of the trip! Soar through the misty cloud forest canopy on one of Costa Rica's most thrilling zip-line circuits. The Original Canopy Tour or Sky Adventures Monteverde offer world-class circuits with up to 15 platforms, Tarzan swings, and rappelling through the forest. Tours last 2.5–3.5 hours and cost $45–85 per person.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Monteverde Butterfly Garden and Insect Museum — explore four different climate zones housing over 30 butterfly species plus a fascinating collection of stick insects, beetles, and leaf-cutter ant colonies. A great 1.5-hour educational experience. ~$15 entry. Follow with a visit to the Don Juan Coffee, Chocolate & Sugar Cane Tour to learn how Costa Rica's famous products are made and enjoy tastings. ~$35.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Santa Elena's vibrant small-town atmosphere. Browse artisan shops for handmade crafts, locally produced coffee, and chocolate. Enjoy a relaxed dinner and live music if available.

meals.breakfast: Lodge breakfast — eggs, gallo pinto, fresh cheese, and coffee before the zip-line tour
meals.lunch: Post-zip-line lunch at a local café in Santa Elena — try Café Colibri for sandwiches, salads, and homemade desserts. ~$10–15
meals.dinner: Dinner at Trio Restaurant in Santa Elena — a popular mid-range spot with creative Costa Rican fusion dishes and excellent local craft beers. ~$18–26 per person

day_by_day.notes: Book the zip-line canopy tour well in advance as it fills up quickly, especially on weekends. Weight limits apply for zip-lining (typically 240–265 lbs maximum). Wear comfortable closed-toe shoes and avoid loose jewelry. The coffee and chocolate tour makes for excellent souvenir shopping opportunities.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning guided birdwatching walk in the Monteverde area — February is peak quetzal season, making this one of the best times of year to spot the resplendent quetzal in its natural habitat. Hire a local guide ($25–40 for 2 hours) for the best chance of sightings. Explore the Curi-Cancha Reserve as an alternative to the main reserve — smaller crowds and excellent wildlife.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depart Monteverde and travel to Arenal Volcano area (approximately 2–3 hours via the Lake Arenal scenic route). Check into a mid-range Arenal lodge with volcano views (options include Arenal Backpackers Resort or Hotel Arenal Manoa at $70–120/night). Afternoon visit to Arenal Volcano National Park for a hike on the lava fields trail with stunning volcano views.
day_by_day.evening: Soak in the natural hot springs fed by Arenal Volcano's geothermal activity. Mid-range options include Baldi Hot Springs or Tabacón (budget option: Eco Termales at $45 per person for a more intimate experience with fewer crowds).

meals.breakfast: Final Monteverde lodge breakfast — enjoy the cool mountain air with a warm cup of locally grown coffee
meals.lunch: Roadside stop en route to Arenal — look for a local soda serving fresh soup and casados. ~$8–12
meals.dinner: Dinner at Don Rufino Restaurant in La Fortuna (Arenal town) — one of the area's best mid-range restaurants with great volcano views and excellent grilled meats. ~$20–30 per person

day_by_day.notes: Overnight stay in Arenal/La Fortuna area. The drive from Monteverde to Arenal via Lake Arenal is one of Costa Rica's most scenic routes — allow extra time for photo stops. Book hot springs in advance, especially Eco Termales which has limited capacity. Bring a swimsuit and towel.

day_by_day.morning: La Fortuna Waterfall hike — take the 500-step descent to the base of the spectacular 75-meter La Fortuna Waterfall for a refreshing swim in the turquoise pool. The hike down takes 20–30 minutes and the entry fee is ~$18. Arrive early to beat the crowds and enjoy the falls in misty morning light.
day_by_day.afternoon: White-water rafting on the Balsa or Sarapiquí River — Arenal is one of Costa Rica's top rafting destinations with options for beginners (Class II–III) and experienced rafters (Class III–IV). Tours last 3–4 hours and cost $55–75 per person including transportation and equipment. An exhilarating eco-adventure experience.
day_by_day.evening: Return to La Fortuna for a relaxed evening. Visit the town's central park and church with the iconic volcano backdrop for photos. Enjoy a street food tour of the local sodas and food carts.

meals.breakfast: Early lodge breakfast before the waterfall hike — eggs, fresh fruit, and strong Costa Rican coffee
meals.lunch: Riverside lunch included with most rafting tours, or stop at a local soda near the river. ~$10–15
meals.dinner: Dinner at Restaurante Nene's in La Fortuna — a beloved local institution serving generous portions of traditional food at very reasonable prices. ~$12–18 per person

day_by_day.notes: For the waterfall, bring water shoes or sandals with grip as the rocks can be slippery. The pool at the base of La Fortuna Waterfall is cold but refreshing. For rafting, listen carefully to the safety briefing and follow your guide's instructions at all times. Secure loose items before entering the raft.

day_by_day.morning: Morning wildlife walk at Caño Negro Wildlife Refuge — a half-day boat tour through this remote wetland refuge (about 1.5 hours from La Fortuna) offers extraordinary wildlife viewing including jabiru storks, roseate spoonbills, anhingas, caiman, river turtles, howler monkeys, and occasionally tapirs. Tours depart around 7:00 AM and cost $55–75 per person.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to La Fortuna and visit the Arenal Hanging Bridges — walk through 16 bridges (6 hanging) suspended over the primary rainforest canopy for a spectacular bird's-eye view of the forest ecosystem. Self-guided tours take 2–3 hours and cost ~$26. Look for toucans, motmots, and sloths in the canopy.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Arenal — transfer back toward the Pacific coast and Aegean Bliss Resort (approximately 3–4 hours). Arrive at the resort in the evening, unpack, and enjoy a welcome-back dinner.

meals.breakfast: Very early lodge breakfast before the Caño Negro tour departure
meals.lunch: Lunch in La Fortuna before departing — try Soda La Parada for hearty, affordable traditional plates. ~$10–14
meals.dinner: Welcome-back dinner at the resort or a nearby beachfront restaurant — treat yourself to a nice seafood platter after days of adventure. ~$22–30 per person

day_by_day.notes: The Caño Negro tour is a full morning commitment — confirm pickup time with your operator the night before. The hanging bridges at Arenal are a great alternative to zip-lining for those wanting a more peaceful canopy experience. The drive back to the coast can be long — download offline maps and bring snacks and water for the road.

day_by_day.morning: Snorkeling or scuba diving excursion from the beach — Costa Rica's Pacific coast offers excellent underwater biodiversity. Join a guided snorkeling boat tour to nearby rocky reefs or islands to spot tropical fish, sea turtles, rays, and possibly dolphins. Tours depart around 8:00 AM and cost $55–85 per person.
day_by_day.afternoon: Surfing lesson on the beach — Costa Rica is one of the world's best surfing destinations and most beach towns have surf schools offering 2-hour beginner lessons for $35–55 per person including board rental. Even non-surfers usually manage to stand up by the end of the lesson!
day_by_day.evening: Spa evening at the resort — book a 60-minute traditional Costa Rican massage using local ingredients like coffee scrub or aloe vera. Many mid-range resorts offer spa services at reasonable prices ($50–80). Followed by a quiet beachfront dinner.

meals.breakfast: Light resort breakfast before the snorkeling tour — fresh fruit, yogurt, and granola. ~$8–12
meals.lunch: Beach lunch at a casual open-air restaurant — fish tacos, ceviche, and a fresh coconut. ~$12–16
meals.dinner: Romantic beachfront dinner — choose a restaurant with tables in the sand, order grilled lobster or shrimp skewers with tropical salsa. ~$25–35 per person

day_by_day.notes: Book snorkeling and surf lessons the day before through the resort or local operators. Bring reef-safe sunscreen for the snorkeling tour to protect marine ecosystems. Beginner surf lessons are suitable for all ages and fitness levels. The spa booking should be made in advance, especially during peak season.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to a nearby national park or protected reserve — options depending on the resort location include Manuel Antonio National Park (known for white-faced capuchin monkeys, sloths, and beautiful beaches), Carara National Park (excellent for scarlet macaws), or Corcovado National Park (the most biodiverse place on Earth). Hire a certified naturalist guide for maximum wildlife sightings.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring the national park — enjoy a swim at a secluded park beach (if applicable), have a picnic lunch, and take final wildlife photos. Return to the resort by mid-afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Final full evening in Costa Rica — take a sunset catamaran cruise along the coast. These 2–3 hour cruises typically include snorkeling, dolphin watching, an open bar, and a gorgeous Pacific sunset. Cost: $65–95 per person. Return to the resort for a farewell dinner.

meals.breakfast: Early resort breakfast before departing for the national park
meals.lunch: Picnic lunch packed by the resort or purchased from a park entrance soda — sandwiches, fruit, and snacks. ~$8–12
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at the best restaurant in the area — splurge slightly on a nice meal to celebrate the trip. Try a seafood tower or whole grilled fish with all the traditional sides. ~$28–40 per person

day_by_day.notes: National park entry fees vary: Manuel Antonio ~$20, Corcovado ~$20–50 depending on zone. Certified naturalist guides cost $25–40 extra but dramatically increase wildlife sighting success. Book the sunset catamaran cruise well in advance as they sell out fast, especially on Fridays. Pack a dry bag for the catamaran cruise.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Costa Rica — wake up early for one last sunrise beach walk or yoga session. Pack your bags and do a final check of the room. Enjoy a long, leisurely last breakfast at the resort. Visit the gift shop for final souvenir purchases — locally made coffee, chocolate, hot sauce, and artisan crafts make excellent gifts.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check out of the resort and transfer to Juan Santamaría International Airport (SJO) — allow 3–4 hours for the journey depending on resort location plus 2–3 hours for international check-in. Browse the airport's duty-free shops for last-minute Costa Rican coffee and rum purchases.
day_by_day.evening: Depart Costa Rica — pura vida! Reflect on 13 incredible days of zip-lining through cloud forests, wildlife safaris in Tortuguero, volcanic hot springs, and pristine Pacific beaches.

meals.breakfast: Final resort breakfast — order everything you loved during the trip one last time. Gallo pinto, fresh tropical fruit, local coffee. ~$10–15
meals.lunch: Early lunch at the resort before checkout or a final stop at a local soda en route to the airport. ~$10–15
meals.dinner: Airport dining at SJO — options include Spoon Restaurant in the terminal for a decent final Costa Rican meal, or save appetite for the flight

day_by_day.notes: Check out time is typically 11:00 AM — confirm with the resort. Allow extra travel time to the airport as Costa Rican traffic can be unpredictable, especially around San José. Keep a small amount of Colones for tips and last-minute purchases. Declare any agricultural products at customs. Pura vida!

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Costa Rica Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

experiences.name: Monteverde Cloud Forest Zip-Line Canopy Tour
experiences.description: Soar through the misty cloud forest canopy on one of Costa Rica's most thrilling zip-line circuits, featuring 15 cables, Tarzan swings, and breathtaking views of the Monteverde reserve. Spot toucans, howler monkeys, and exotic orchids along the way.

experiences.name: Tortuguero National Park Wildlife Boat Safari
experiences.description: Glide through the jungle canals of Tortuguero on a guided boat safari teeming with caimans, river turtles, three-toed sloths, poison dart frogs, and over 300 bird species. Depending on the season, witness the awe-inspiring nesting of green sea turtles on the beach.

experiences.name: Arenal Volcano Hanging Bridges Hike
experiences.description: Trek through primary rainforest on a network of 16 hanging bridges suspended high above the forest floor, offering panoramic views of Arenal Volcano and incredible wildlife encounters including poison dart frogs, coatis, and resplendent quetzals.

experiences.name: Manuel Antonio Beach and Wildlife Snorkel Experience
experiences.description: Combine a relaxing afternoon on the pristine white-sand beaches of Manuel Antonio National Park with a guided snorkeling session in the warm Pacific waters. Encounter white-faced capuchin monkeys, sloths, and colorful reef fish just steps from the shoreline.

experiences.name: Corcovado National Park Guided Jungle Trek
experiences.description: Explore one of the most biodiverse places on Earth with a certified naturalist guide deep into Corcovado's old-growth rainforest. Encounter tapirs, scarlet macaws, white-lipped peccaries, and jaguar tracks on this immersive full-day eco-adventure in the Osa Peninsula.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Juan Santamaría International Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Private luxury transfer arranged to Aegean Bliss Resort Beachfront property.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private luxury transfer from San José airport to the resort (approximately 2–4 hours depending on location). Scenic drive through Costa Rica's lush central valley. Champagne and cold towel welcome upon arrival. Check-in, resort orientation tour, and time to settle into your beachfront suite.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails on your private terrace or the resort's beachfront bar. Welcome dinner at the resort's signature fine-dining restaurant showcasing Costa Rican coastal cuisine with fresh Pacific seafood.

meals.breakfast: N/A — in-flight or airport lounge
meals.lunch: Light snack or airport lounge dining pre-departure or en route
meals.dinner: Resort signature restaurant — 'La Costa Table': tasting menu featuring ceviche de corvina, grilled pargo rojo, and tropical fruit dessert pairing with local guaro cocktails

day_by_day.notes: Ensure private airport transfer is pre-booked with resort concierge. Request early room preparation given afternoon arrival. Pack light for first evening — luggage delivered to room by butler service.

day_by_day.morning: Leisurely resort breakfast followed by a guided sunrise beach walk along the resort's private coastline. Naturalist guide introduces local coastal wildlife including scarlet macaws, white-faced capuchin monkeys, and shorebirds commonly spotted at dawn.
day_by_day.afternoon: Manuel Antonio Beach and Wildlife Snorkel Experience — explore the pristine white-sand beaches of Manuel Antonio National Park combined with a guided snorkel session in the crystal-clear Pacific waters. Spot parrotfish, angelfish, and vibrant coral formations. A certified naturalist guide accompanies the group through the park's jungle trails to observe sloths, iguanas, and squirrel monkeys.
day_by_day.evening: Return to resort for sunset yoga session on the beachfront deck. Pre-dinner spa treatment — signature 'Rainforest Renewal' 60-minute massage using local volcanic clay and tropical botanicals.

meals.breakfast: Resort beachfront breakfast pavilion — fresh tropical fruit platters, gallo pinto, eggs Benedict with smoked marlin, freshly brewed Costa Rican coffee
meals.lunch: Beachside picnic curated by resort chef — artisan sandwiches, ceviche cups, fresh coconut water, and tropical fruit served at Manuel Antonio
meals.dinner: Candlelit dinner at resort's oceanfront terrace restaurant — grilled whole red snapper, hearts of palm salad, and chocolate-chili lava cake

day_by_day.notes: Wear reef-safe sunscreen for snorkeling. Bring waterproof bag for electronics. Manuel Antonio is a short distance from most beachfront resorts on the central Pacific coast — confirm exact transfer time with concierge.

day_by_day.morning: Private catamaran sunrise cruise along the Pacific coastline. Spot dolphins, sea turtles, and humpback whales (February is peak whale-watching season). Champagne breakfast served on deck with panoramic ocean views.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to resort. Afternoon at leisure — enjoy the infinity pool, beachfront hammocks, or book a private surf lesson with the resort's certified instructor on the resort's beach break.
day_by_day.evening: Private beachfire dinner experience — personal chef prepares a 5-course meal on the beach under the stars. Menu features locally sourced ingredients: fresh oysters, lobster thermidor, and tropical sorbet.

meals.breakfast: Champagne breakfast served aboard the private catamaran — smoked salmon, croissants, tropical fruit, and mimosas
meals.lunch: Resort pool bar — gourmet burgers, fresh guacamole with plantain chips, and fresh-squeezed juices
meals.dinner: Exclusive private beach dinner for two — 5-course chef's tasting menu with wine pairing (pre-book 48 hours in advance with resort concierge)

day_by_day.notes: February is excellent for whale-watching — humpback whales migrate through Costa Rica's Pacific coast during this period. Book catamaran in advance through resort activities desk.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning transfer departs resort toward Arenal Volcano region (approximately 3–4 hours). Scenic mountain road journey through coffee plantations and cloud forest. Stop at a premium artisan coffee estate for a private cupping and tour.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arenal Volcano Hanging Bridges Hike — trek through primary rainforest on a network of 16 hanging bridges suspended high above the forest floor. Certified naturalist guide identifies poison dart frogs, toucans, howler monkeys, and rare orchids. Panoramic views of Arenal Volcano from elevated bridge platforms.
day_by_day.evening: Check-in at luxury Arenal-area lodge (pre-arranged by resort concierge as an overnight excursion property). Soak in natural volcanic hot springs at a premium thermal pool complex with volcano views. Cocktails and dinner overlooking the illuminated volcano.

meals.breakfast: Early continental breakfast at resort before departure — pastries, fruit, and coffee to go
meals.lunch: Lunch at premium open-air restaurant near Arenal — casado with local beef tenderloin, fresh salad, and natural fruit juice
meals.dinner: Fine dining at Arenal lodge restaurant — volcanic stone-grilled meats, local cheese board, and traditional tres leches dessert with a glass of Chilean Carménère

day_by_day.notes: This is an overnight excursion — pack an overnight bag. Arenal Volcano National Park requires advance entry reservation. Hanging bridges hike is moderate difficulty — wear closed-toe hiking shoes and bring insect repellent.

day_by_day.morning: Sunrise kayaking on Lake Arenal — paddle across the glassy volcanic lake with views of Arenal Volcano at dawn. Guided by a local naturalist who points out kingfishers, herons, and lake wildlife. Optional: stand-up paddleboard alternative available.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private transfer continues north toward Tortuguero region (approximately 4–5 hours including boat transfer through jungle canals). Arrive at luxury eco-lodge deep within Tortuguero's canal network.
day_by_day.evening: Welcome briefing from Tortuguero eco-lodge naturalist guide. Nighttime jungle walk along resort grounds — spot tree frogs, sleeping birds, and nocturnal insects. Dinner at lodge's open-air rainforest restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Full hot breakfast at Arenal lodge before departure — scrambled eggs, plantains, fresh fruit, and Costa Rican coffee
meals.lunch: Packed gourmet lunch enjoyed during boat transfer through Tortuguero canals — sandwiches, fresh fruit, and sparkling water
meals.dinner: Tortuguero eco-lodge restaurant — Caribbean-style rice and beans with coconut milk, grilled mahi-mahi, and plantain tostones

day_by_day.notes: Tortuguero is only accessible by boat or small plane — all transfers coordinated through concierge. Pack light dry bags as boat travel through canals may encounter light rain. February is low-rain season but afternoon showers possible.

day_by_day.morning: Tortuguero National Park Wildlife Boat Safari — glide through the jungle canals of Tortuguero on a guided private boat safari. Spot caimans basking on riverbanks, river turtles, Jesus Christ lizards, three-toed sloths, and an extraordinary array of tropical birds including toucans, kingfishers, and great green macaws.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to eco-lodge for lunch. Afternoon guided walk through Tortuguero village — learn about the local Caribbean community's conservation efforts and sea turtle protection programs. Visit the Caribbean Conservation Corporation visitor center.
day_by_day.evening: Sundowner cocktails on the lodge's canal-side deck. Optional: nighttime guided beach walk to observe nesting sea turtles (subject to seasonal availability — February may have limited nesting activity; green turtles nest primarily July–October, but leatherbacks begin arriving February–March).

meals.breakfast: Sunrise breakfast at lodge — fresh papaya, pineapple, rice and beans, eggs, and strong Costa Rican coffee served overlooking the canal
meals.lunch: Lodge restaurant — Caribbean lobster soup, fresh ceviche, and coconut flan
meals.dinner: Private candlelit dinner on the lodge's canal deck — whole grilled Caribbean snapper, coconut curry vegetables, and rum-infused pineapple dessert

day_by_day.notes: Bring binoculars for the boat safari — wildlife sightings are exceptional in the early morning hours. Wear neutral-colored, lightweight clothing. Apply DEET-based insect repellent before canal tours.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning birdwatching walk with lodge ornithologist — Tortuguero is a globally recognized birding destination with over 300 recorded species. Spot montezuma oropendolas, snowy egrets, and roseate spoonbills in the canal-side vegetation.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private boat transfer back to mainland. Luxury vehicle transfer south toward Monteverde Cloud Forest region (approximately 4–5 hours). Arrive at premium Monteverde boutique lodge perched above the cloud forest canopy.
day_by_day.evening: Check-in and settle into cloud forest lodge suite with panoramic misty forest views. Sunset wine and cheese reception hosted by lodge naturalist who briefs guests on the following day's zip-line adventure. Dinner at lodge's renowned farm-to-table restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Final Tortuguero breakfast — tropical smoothie bowls, fresh bread, and Caribbean-spiced scrambled eggs
meals.lunch: Roadside stop at premium Costa Rican countryside restaurant — traditional casado, fresh agua dulce, and local cheese
meals.dinner: Monteverde lodge farm-to-table restaurant — cloud forest mushroom risotto, grass-fed beef tenderloin, and artisan cheese board sourced from local Monteverde dairy farms

day_by_day.notes: Monteverde roads are partially unpaved — transfer vehicle will be a premium 4WD. Temperatures in Monteverde average 65–72°F (18–22°C) — pack a light layer and waterproof jacket.

day_by_day.morning: Monteverde Cloud Forest Zip-Line Canopy Tour — soar through the misty cloud forest canopy on one of Costa Rica's most thrilling zip-line circuits. Experience multiple platforms, Tarzan swings, and a Superman-style cable suspended above the ancient cloud forest. Expert guides provide safety briefings and natural history commentary throughout.
day_by_day.afternoon: Guided walk through the Santa Elena Cloud Forest Reserve — a quieter, less-visited alternative to the main Monteverde reserve. Spot resplendent quetzals (February is pre-nesting season — excellent sighting probability), emerald toucanets, and rare cloud forest orchids with a certified birding guide.
day_by_day.evening: Night tour of Monteverde Cloud Forest with a herpetologist guide — spotlight nocturnal wildlife including red-eyed tree frogs, glass frogs, sleeping hummingbirds, and kinkajous. Return to lodge for a warming nightcap of local guaro sour.

meals.breakfast: Hearty pre-adventure breakfast at lodge — eggs any style, gallo pinto, fresh fruit, granola, and Costa Rican pour-over coffee
meals.lunch: Post-zip-line lunch at canopy tour company's open-air restaurant — wood-fired pizza, fresh salads, and tropical fruit smoothies
meals.dinner: Lodge chef's special 4-course dinner — cream of chayote soup, cloud forest hearts of palm salad, slow-braised local lamb, and passion fruit panna cotta

day_by_day.notes: Zip-line tour requires closed-toe shoes and comfortable athletic wear. Weight restrictions typically apply (15–120 kg) — confirm with operator. Quetzal sightings are most likely at dawn near fruiting aguacatillo trees — consider an optional 5:30 AM quetzal walk.

day_by_day.morning: Private coffee and chocolate tour at a premium organic Monteverde farm. Learn about Costa Rica's world-renowned arabica coffee cultivation and single-origin chocolate production. Guided tasting of estate-grown coffees paired with artisan dark chocolates.
day_by_day.afternoon: Transfer south toward Corcovado National Park region on the Osa Peninsula (approximately 5–6 hours or 45-minute private charter flight — strongly recommended). Arrive at luxury eco-lodge adjacent to Corcovado's park entrance.
day_by_day.evening: Briefing with Corcovado naturalist guide over cocktails. Review wildlife checklist — tapirs, jaguars, scarlet macaws, and all four Costa Rican monkey species are regularly sighted. Early dinner and early bedtime in preparation for a full day in Corcovado.

meals.breakfast: Coffee farm breakfast — fresh-brewed estate coffee, local bread with homemade jams, tropical fruit, and farm eggs
meals.lunch: In-transit or at charter flight terminal — gourmet packed lunch prepared by Monteverde lodge
meals.dinner: Osa Peninsula eco-lodge restaurant — fresh local catch of the day, yuca fries, tropical salad, and homemade coconut ice cream

day_by_day.notes: Private charter flight from Monteverde/San José to Puerto Jiménez (Drake Bay) is highly recommended — saves significant travel time and provides spectacular aerial views of the Osa Peninsula. Book well in advance. Corcovado entry requires advance park reservation and certified guide.

day_by_day.morning: Corcovado National Park Guided Jungle Trek — full-day expedition into one of the most biodiverse places on Earth with a certified naturalist guide. Morning trek deep into Corcovado's primary rainforest along the Sirena trail system. Wildlife targets include Baird's tapir, white-lipped peccaries, scarlet macaws, and the elusive jaguar.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue jungle trek — reach the remote Sirena Biological Station for a rest stop. Afternoon wildlife tracking with guide along river corridors where tapirs and peccaries regularly drink. Spot giant anteaters, bull sharks in the river (observed safely from banks), and extraordinary insect life.
day_by_day.evening: Boat transfer back to eco-lodge along the Osa coastline at sunset — watch scarlet macaws fly in pairs overhead. Arrive back at lodge for a well-deserved hot shower, therapeutic massage, and celebratory dinner.

meals.breakfast: Pre-dawn breakfast at lodge — energy-rich oatmeal, eggs, fruit, and coffee before 6:00 AM departure
meals.lunch: Packed gourmet lunch at Sirena Station — sandwiches, energy bars, fresh fruit, and ample hydration
meals.dinner: Lodge celebration dinner — whole roasted chicken with chimichurri, grilled vegetables, patacones, and a bottle of premium South American red wine

day_by_day.notes: Corcovado is physically demanding — wear broken-in waterproof hiking boots, long lightweight pants, and bring 3+ liters of water. Leech socks recommended. This is a bucket-list wildlife experience — February dry season offers excellent trail conditions and wildlife concentration around water sources.

day_by_day.morning: Sunrise dolphin and whale-watching boat tour from Drake Bay — the Osa Peninsula's waters are renowned for year-round dolphin pods (spinner and bottlenose) and February humpback whale sightings. Snorkeling stop at Isla del Caño Biological Reserve — one of Costa Rica's premier dive sites with exceptional visibility.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Osa eco-lodge. Afternoon at leisure — relax on the lodge's jungle-edge infinity pool, enjoy a rainforest spa treatment, or join an optional mangrove kayak tour through the lodge's private coastal waterway.
day_by_day.evening: Private charter flight back to the main Pacific coast (approximately 45 minutes) and luxury transfer back to Aegean Bliss Resort. Welcome-back cocktail awaits. Dinner at resort.

meals.breakfast: Early light breakfast at Osa lodge before boat departure — fruit, yogurt, and coffee
meals.lunch: Fresh ceviche and grilled fish lunch at Drake Bay waterfront restaurant with Pacific Ocean views
meals.dinner: Return dinner at Aegean Bliss Resort — seafood paella for two, crispy calamari, and mango sorbet with a glass of Spanish Albariño

day_by_day.notes: Isla del Caño snorkeling requires reef-safe sunscreen. Visibility is typically 20–30 meters in February — ideal conditions. Confirm return charter flight timing with concierge to ensure smooth transfer back to resort.

day_by_day.morning: Full resort morning — sleep in and enjoy a leisurely breakfast at the resort. Book a private yoga and meditation session on the beachfront pavilion with the resort's resident wellness instructor. Optional: stand-up paddleboarding on calm morning Pacific waters.
day_by_day.afternoon: Premium spa day at the resort's full-service spa — book a 2-hour 'Pura Vida Ritual' package including volcanic mud wrap, hot stone massage, and botanical facial using locally sourced ingredients. Followed by pool time and fresh tropical juice service.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktail masterclass with the resort's head mixologist — learn to craft classic Costa Rican cocktails including the guaro sour, coco loco, and tamarind margarita. Farewell dinner at the resort's premier fine-dining venue.

meals.breakfast: Indulgent resort breakfast in bed — full continental spread with fresh-baked pastries, smoked salmon, tropical fruits, and Chemex-brewed single-origin Costa Rican coffee
meals.lunch: Pool-side gourmet lunch — tuna poke bowl, lobster roll, fresh açaí bowl, and sparkling water with citrus
meals.dinner: Resort premier fine-dining restaurant — 7-course chef's tasting menu with wine pairing: amuse-bouche, tuna tartare, hearts of palm bisque, mango sorbet intermezzo, wagyu beef tenderloin, local cheese selection, and chocolate ganache with gold leaf

day_by_day.notes: Spa treatments should be booked 24–48 hours in advance. This is a designated rest and recovery day after the intensive Corcovado and Tortuguero expeditions. Use the afternoon to pack and prepare for departure the following morning.

day_by_day.morning: Final sunrise beach walk along the resort's private coastline — a peaceful last moment with Costa Rica's Pacific biodiversity. Spot scarlet macaws, pelicans, and perhaps a final sloth sighting in the resort's garden trees. Checkout and luggage handling by resort butler.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private luxury transfer to Juan Santamaría International Airport. En route, optional stop at a premium artisan market in San José for last-minute souvenirs — locally produced coffee, artisan chocolates, handcrafted jewelry, and traditional ceramics. Airport lounge access arranged by resort concierge.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Costa Rica with extraordinary memories of cloud forests, volcanic landscapes, pristine Pacific beaches, and unparalleled wildlife encounters. Pura Vida!

meals.breakfast: Final resort breakfast — full Costa Rican spread with gallo pinto, fresh tropical fruits, pastries, eggs, and a final cup of world-class Costa Rican coffee
meals.lunch: San José premium airport lounge or La Esquina de Buenos Aires restaurant near the airport — Argentine-style grill with Costa Rican touches
meals.dinner: In-flight dining or airport lounge

day_by_day.notes: Allow minimum 3 hours before international departure for check-in and security. Resort concierge will coordinate luggage and transfer timing. Consider purchasing vacuum-sealed bags of premium Costa Rican coffee directly from resort gift shop as a final keepsake. Confirm duty-free allowances for bringing back local spirits and chocolates.

query: Costa Rica eco-adventure, $2500, zip-lining and wildlife, February 2026 from Miami
